Chander Negi, Judge
Whether approved for reporting?

For the Petitioner : Mr.
Rupinder Singh and Mr. Ashwani Negi, Advocates.

For the Respondent : Mr. Raj Kumar Negi, Additional Advocate General Psi Balbir Singh is present
alongwith record Bipin Chander Negi Judge (oral) Status report stands filed.

2. The petitioner has filed the present application, under Section 438 of Code of Criminal Procedure
(hereinafter referred to as 'the Cr.P.C.') in case Fir No. 279 of 2023, dated 28.11.2023, under
Sections 406 & 420 of the Indian Penal Code (hereinafter referred to as 'the Ipc") registered with
Police Station, Bilaspur District Bilaspur, H.P. .
3.

The petitioner has sought the indulgence of this Court to direct the Investigating Officer/Police, to release him on bail, in the event of his arrest, in the abovementioned case, as, he is apprehending his arrest, in the said case.
4.
According to the petitioner, he has been falsely implicated in the present case, as he is innocent person and has nothing to do with the case.

5. According to the petitioner, nothing is to be recovered from him nor his custody is warranted in this case.
6.
On all these submissions, Mr. Rupinder Singh Advocate has prayed that the bail application may kindly be allowed.

7. On 7.12.2023, interim direction was issued to the Investigating Officer to release the petitioner on bail, in case 279 of 2023, dated 28.11.2023, in the event of his arrest, subject to his furnishing bail bonds, in the sum of Rs.
25,000/ with one surety, in the like amount, to the satisfaction of the Investigating Officer.
8. In the status report so filed, it has been disclosed .
therein that on 27.11.2023, complainant Vishal Nadda appeared before the Police and moved the complaint disclosing therein that legal action be taken against the SMB Jeevan Saharsh Nidhi Limited.

sentences.text: According to the petitioner, he is resident of the address, as mentioned in the application.
The complainant has deposited a sum of Rs. 31979/in the Company, which is having its office at Ghumarwin, near Bank of Baroda in the house of one Vikrant Panda.
There are other persons who have also deposited amounts with the said company.
10. According to the complainant, he came to know that the Company has closed its office.
11. It is the further case of the complainant that the company has falsely allured people and misappropriated the amount, deposited by common people.
Hence, the complainant has prayed that the action be taken against the company.

12. On this, the Police registered the case against the .
petitioner and criminal machinery swung into motion.
13. Investigation of the case was entrusted to the Assistant SubInspector, Rajesh Kumar.

During investigation, the Police has taken into possession the entire records w.r.t Recurring Deposit, saving accounts, fixed deposits, loans given by the Company and user ID, password for operating the online transaction of the company.
The Police had also inquired from the persons, residing within the territorial jurisdiction of Police Station, Bilaspur, who had allegedly invested their money with the aforesaid Bank.

Their statements were recorded under Section 161 of the Cr. P.C.
14.
As per their statements, the agents of the Company used to collect money from people for depositing the same in the recurring deposit, fixed deposits.
They also used to collect money for depositing the same in the saving bank account of the people.

But, after the date of maturity, the amount collected from the people has not been returned back, as such, they have cheated the people,
for lacs of rupees.

15. From a perusal of the status report filed today, it .
is evident that according to the petitioner besides collecting deposits in the form of fixed deposit recurring deposits and saving account the company in question had also been disbursing the loan.
The loan so disbursed has not been recovered till date.

16.. Learned counsel appearing on behalf of the petitioner has submitted that the main accused Atul Kumar in a FIR bearing No. 216 of 2023, dated 27.11.2023, under Sections 406 and 420 of I.P.C.
registered at Police Station Ghumarwin, District Bilaspur with respect to the operations of the company in question has been enlarged on regular bail under Section 439 Cr.P.C vide judgment dated 16.1.2024.
17.
On the basis of above facts, a prayer has been made to dismiss the bail application.
18. Heard.

sentences.text:
The petitioner has joined investigation, as per the directions issued by this Court, and has been released on bail, by the Investigating Officer, as per the directions issued by .
this Court.
20. The role, allegedly played by the petitioner, in the commission of offences, will be proved during the trial.

At the time of deciding the bail application, the detailed discussion about the material collected by the I.O. should be avoided, as it would cause prejudice to the case of prosecution or to the case of accused.

21. The application cannot be dismissed, as a matter of punishment, as pretrial punishment, is prohibited under the law, and the petitioner is presumed to be innocent, till the conclusion of the trial.

22. Considering all these facts, this Court is of the view that the Police has not been able to make out a case for custodial interrogation of the petitioner, as such, the interim order dated 7.12.2023 is liable to be made absolute.

23. Consequently, interim order dated 7.12.2023 is made absolute subject to the following conditions:
a)That the petitioner will join the investigation of the .
case as and when, called for, by the Investigating Officer, in accordance with law;
b) That the petitioner will not leave India, without prior permission of the Court.

c) That the petitioner will not, directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person, acquainted with the facts of the case, so as to dissuade him/her from disclosing such facts to the Investigating Officer or the Court; and d) That the petitioner shall regularly attend the trial Court on each and every date of hearing and if prevented by any reason to do so, seek exemption from appearance by filing appropriate application."
24.
In view of above, the bail application is, thus, disposed of.

25. Any of the observations, made hereinabove, shall not be taken as an expression of opinion, on the merits of the case, as these observations, are confined, only, to the disposal of the present bail application.
26. The petitioner is directed to move regular bail application, when charge sheet will be filed in the Competent Court of law.
